# Migration Readiness Checklist: Migrate Build Artifacts to AWS Artifactory

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements for the cutover lifecycle (what moves, fallback,
rollback, retirement) and the access model (identities, permissions, secrets) are complete, clear,
consistent, and measurable, for the spec and plan review before `/speckit-tasks`
**Created**: 2026-10-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Does FR-022 say whether in-scope artifacts stay readable across a rollback: those
  published to the new location before it, and those published to the old location while rolled
  back? Reuse, history tools, and runs in progress depend on them, and research R7 assumes both
  stay readable. [Gap, Spec §FR-022, §FR-016, Research R7]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are a rollback trigger and a decision owner defined (which failures or outage
  length justify rolling back, and who decides), so that the one-hour limit in FR-022 and SC-009
  has a defined start? [Gap, Spec §FR-022, §SC-009]
  - Note (2026-10-14): Partly addressed: FR-022 names CI administrators as the owner; no rollback trigger is defined yet.
- [ ] CHK003 - Does FR-014 define the outcome when the fallback request to the old location fails
  for a reason other than absence (rejected, unreachable, retired)? Does that outcome match the
  edge case that treats builds on a retired old repository like builds deleted by retention?
  [Gap, Conflict, Spec §FR-014, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the metadata that pipelines attach today listed (which properties, on which
  artifacts), and does FR-004 also cover metadata attached or changed after the first publish?
  [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK005 - Does FR-013 say where token expiry dates and renewal owners are recorded? Does it
  require a warning before expiry and a rotation that causes no CI outage, not only a clean failure
  afterwards? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
  - Note (2026-10-14): Partly addressed: FR-013 records expiry and owner in internal documentation; advance warning and outage-free rotation are not required yet.
- [ ] CHK006 - Does FR-020's list of environment classes (build agents, containerized test agents,
  remote GPU test clusters) cover every place that touches in-scope artifacts? Research R1 also
  lists Jenkins agents (property lookups, coverage selection), container-image build pods, and the
  cluster that publishes profile-optimized builds. Is "each remote GPU test cluster" an enumerated
  list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, Research R1]
- [ ] CHK007 - Are observability requirements defined in both directions: where each in-scope
  artifact was published, and where and in what form FR-014's "record which location served it" is
  kept? SC-001 and the missed-reader edge case need that evidence.
  [Gap, Spec §FR-002, §FR-014, §SC-001]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 - Does FR-001's "packaged builds that the build stages produce" settle the borderline
  archives: profile-optimized builds that profile generation publishes outside the build stages,
  and source release packages whose producer is unknown?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Research R1, Research R13]
- [x] CHK009 - Does the spec say which pipeline code version decides where a run publishes and
  reads? This matters for merge-request runs of PRs opened before the merge, for the change's own
  pre-merge runs (which already publish to the new location, per quickstart step 3), and for jobs
  that a pre-merge run triggers after the merge. Without it, "cutover is the merge" has more than
  one meaning. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-006, Research R12]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are "fails quickly" (Edge Cases) and "within its normal retry budget" (FR-013) one
  rule? Is it stated whether an authentication failure is retried at all?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 - Does "make that build's artifacts available to the current run" mean copied into the
  current run's directory, or read in place from the earlier build's location?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK012 - Does FR-024 define how "known consumers outside this repository" are found, the
  minimum notice before the merge, and what happens to consumers that have not switched by then?
  Because FR-002 rules out dual publishing, they stop receiving new builds at the merge.
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-024, §FR-002, Research R10]
- [x] CHK013 - Can FR-010 be signed off as written? Its operation list ends in "such as", so the
  publishing identity's permissions are an open set, and it names no evidence for
  distribution-list membership, portal issuance, or storage in the credential store.
  [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-010, §FR-020]
  - Note (2026-10-14): Partly addressed: FR-010 now lists exactly four permissions; it still names no evidence for list membership, portal issuance, or credential storage.
- [x] CHK014 - Is "destination" defined (the whole `sw-tensorrt-llm-generic-local` repository, or
  its `llm-artifacts/` path)? Are "location", "repository", and "instance" used consistently where
  the difference matters, as in the permissions of FR-010 and FR-011 and in retiring the "old
  repository" versus the old instance? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §Key Entities]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK015 - Do FR-019 and SC-007 allow for the functional old-location references that the
  design keeps on purpose, namely the FR-014 fallback and the FR-022 rollback target? Both permit
  only non-functional references, and the data model adds a `fallback` disposition that the spec
  does not define. [Conflict, Spec §FR-019, §SC-007, §FR-014, Data model §Artifact reference]
- [x] CHK016 - Are FR-005 ("look in the new location first"), SC-001, and SC-002 reconciled with
  the FR-022 rollback? That needs the read order while rolled back, and how runs during a rollback
  count toward the success criteria. [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §SC-001, §SC-002, §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK017 - Can the missed-reader edge case (the old repository's access records show no
  remaining requests from TRT-LLM CI) hold while the FR-014 fallback deliberately reads
  pre-cutover builds there and out-of-scope artifacts stay there? Is the check limited to the paths
  of post-cutover builds, or otherwise able to tell these requests apart?
  [Conflict, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-014, §FR-001]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the spec's assumption that moving the build_info.txt and waive_list/ uploads
  requires a shared CI library change updated to match the plan, which publishes them from this
  repository? Is the dependency on the library's owners still accurate?
  [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions, §Dependencies, Research R2]
- [x] CHK019 - Are FR-008 and FR-013 reconciled with the rule that internal names stay out of
  repository files? They require tool messages and developer documentation to explain
  distribution-list membership, the self-service portal, and renewal. Does the spec say where that
  guidance lives and what in-repository text may say?
  [Conflict, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013, Research R11]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK020 - Is FR-021's baseline unambiguous: which pre-cutover run counts as "the same commit",
  when every run of the merge commit already contains the change?
  [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021, §US2]
- [ ] CHK021 - Can SC-002 be measured: is there a stated way to attribute a run failure to an
  in-scope publish or fetch, and to separate it from an "outage of the new instance itself"?
  [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK022 - Does SC-006 define its log scan: which sources (including job logs on remote GPU
  clusters, and published artifacts) and how an exposed token is detected?
  [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is the SC-007 search defined well enough to find indirect references (URLs built from
  variables, repository names derived by string manipulation)? Is the reference inventory linked
  as the denominator for "every" in FR-005 and FR-019?
  [Measurability, Traceability, Spec §SC-007, §FR-005, §FR-019, Research R1]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK024 - Do FR-006 and the in-progress-run edge case cover runs in progress when a rollback
  or roll-forward takes effect? Is a run allowed to split its artifacts across both locations,
  which the plan permits by resolving the switch once per step?
  [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, §FR-022, Contract §Primary and secondary]
- [ ] CHK025 - Is the per-branch rollout covered: does each branch that adopts the change get its
  own FR-024 notice, FR-020 verification, and FR-021 comparison, or does only main?
  [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, §FR-020, §FR-021, §FR-024]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK026 - Does the spec define how "absent" is told apart from "not permitted" when the
  instance may answer unauthorized requests with "not found"? Artifactory can be configured to hide
  unauthorized resources that way, and then a missing permission would trigger the FR-014 fallback,
  which rejected credentials must never trigger. [Edge Case, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK027 - Does FR-012's "after a job ends" include abnormal endings (cancellation, timeout,
  node failure), when cleanup steps on remote GPU cluster hosts may not run?
  [Edge Case, Spec §FR-012, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK028 - Are throttling responses from the new instance (for example HTTP 429) addressed:
  whether they count as transient failures, and whether dozens of parallel stages sharing one
  reader identity stay within the instance's limits? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK029 - Does FR-012 cover exposure channels beyond logs, published artifacts, links, and
  leftover files? Examples are process command lines and environments visible to other users of a
  shared host, and container image layers built while a token is present.
  [Coverage, Security, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK030 - Does the spec say which environments may hold the publishing identity, and whether
  environments that run contributor-controlled code (PR builds and tests) may hold it? That
  identity can overwrite other runs' artifacts. [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-010, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK031 - Does the spec require each instance's credentials to go only to that instance: never
  to the old instance during fallback, and never to another host that a download is redirected to?
  [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-009, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK032 - Are transfer-time expectations quantified? That covers the "existing pipeline time
  limits" in the large-transfer edge case, and a per-environment measure, since SC-003's
  whole-pipeline median also moves with test-list and CI-load changes. The plan's 10%
  per-environment threshold (research R14) is not in the spec.
  [Clarity, Performance, Spec §Edge Cases, §SC-003, Research R14]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK033 - Is it recorded, and agreed with the program, that it will sign off a migration of
  three artifact types even though its guide asks for every urm.nvidia.com reference to be
  repointed? [Assumption, Spec §FR-023, §SC-008, §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK034 - Is the old repository's retirement date, or the end of the transition window,
  documented, along with the assumption that anonymous reads stay enabled there until then? The
  FR-014 fallback (anonymous, per FR-009), the FR-022 rollback, and the SC-008 deadline depend on
  it. [Assumption, Spec §SC-008, §FR-009, §FR-022, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK035 - Is an owner named for the out-of-scope llm-artifacts outputs that have no follow-up
  ticket (coverage archives, HTML reports, scan logs, image-tag maps, shared stores)? The old
  repository cannot be retired until they move. [Dependency, Gap, Spec §Out of scope, §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK036 - Is the old repository's retention policy stated concretely (age or count rules), so
  that "retention on the new repository matches" can be checked? Is the program's commitment to
  configure it recorded? [Assumption, Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK037 - Are storage capacity on the destination (package size × runs per day × retention)
  and reachability of the new instance from every execution environment, including remote GPU
  clusters with restricted egress, stated as assumptions with owners?
  [Assumption, Gap, Spec §Assumptions, §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is the blast radius of reusing the existing image identities addressed? The spec
  proposes the image-pull identity for reading and the plan reuses the image-push identity for
  publishing, so one revoked or rotated token would stop both image traffic and artifact access.
  [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Research R5]
- [ ] CHK039 - Is FR-017 scoped consistently with FR-001: does it cover build-info records for
  everything these pipelines publish, or only records describing in-scope artifacts? If records
  exist, does the spec say how migrating them fits FR-014's no-copy decision, given they would
  describe files absent from the new instance? [Conflict, Spec §FR-017, §FR-014, §FR-001]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK040 - Are the two pending decisions resolved, or each tied to a rollout gate? They are
  FR-018's open marker (main only, or release branches too) and FR-014's no-copy approach, which
  still awaits confirmation. [Ambiguity, Dependency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-014, §Clarifications]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Reference key: `Spec §` cites [spec.md](../spec.md), `Research R` cites
  [research.md](../research.md), `Data model §` cites [data-model.md](../data-model.md), and
  `Contract §` cites [contracts/artifact-locations.md](../contracts/artifact-locations.md).
- Some items flag questions that the plan already answers but the spec does not yet state, for
  example CHK001, CHK018, CHK019, CHK024, and CHK032. Resolve those by updating the spec.
